evals.prompt:
We are adding project tracking to an existing Twenty CRM app. The app's source root is src/ and it already depends on twenty-sdk. I want to define these objects in one TypeScript file and scaffold them with @saeidex/t20:

- Project: title (text), budget (number), status (one of active/paused/done), tags (fixed choices: internal, client, urgent), client (one Client), teams (many Team)
- Client: company (text), projects (many Project)
- Team: name (text), projects (many Project)

Write the exact input file (types.ts), the exact t20 command you would run (output to src, stable IDs), and a short report explaining:
1. which objects/files t20 will generate, including any object you did not declare;
2. anything in the plan that will NOT behave as a naive user expects;
3. how the user should actually execute it given the CLI's interaction model.

Do not run the interactive CLI. Save types.ts and report.md under outputs/. You may inspect the repo at C:\Users\EK Nayeem\code\t20 for ground truth.
evals.expected_output: A types.ts with Project/Client/Team using reciprocal arrays for the Project-Team many-to-many, a command with -i/-o/--seed, and a report that mentions the synthesized ProjectTeam junction, interactive object selection, and field/naming quirks.
assertions: types.ts declares Project, Client, and Team as top-level types/interfaces in one file
Project and Team use reciprocal array relations (or otherwise intentionally trigger t20's many-to-many junction), not a hand-written junction type
Report says t20 synthesizes an extra junction object (e.g. ProjectTeam) for the many-to-many
Report notes that object selection is always interactive and there is no non-interactive selection flag
Report predicts the generated output directories (objects/views/navigation-menu-items) and per-object file names
Report does not assume a declared `name` field on Project/Team will be generated (id/name are skipped)

evals.prompt:
We use @saeidex/t20 0.8.19 to scaffold a Twenty app. Input file: C:\Users\EK Nayeem\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\t20-workspace\fixtures\order-types.ts
Generated object: C:\Users\EK Nayeem\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\t20-workspace\fixtures\generated\objects\order.object.ts
CI log: C:\Users\EK Nayeem\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\t20-workspace\fixtures\ci-log.txt

Three things look wrong:
- orderId is generated as FieldType.TEXT, but we expected UUID.
- --dry-run prints 'undefined' blocks.
- tsc fails on generated imports with backslashes on Windows.

Diagnose each from the actual implementation and give concrete fixes/workarounds. Also say whether the repository README can be trusted for these behaviors. Save report.md under outputs/. Do not modify repo files.
evals.expected_output: A report explaining the literal lowercase id/uppercase ID heuristic and dead *Id branch, the resultOutput shape mismatch, the Windows path.relative backslash issue, and README drift.
assertions: Explains that orderId is TEXT because the heuristic matches only literal lowercase `id` or uppercase `ID` (camelCase `Id` does not match)
Mentions the *Id suffix branch is dead/unreachable or otherwise says declaring FieldType.UUID explicitly is the fix
Identifies the --dry-run/--print bug as a mismatch between resultOutput expecting {content,file} and generateResult returning {[filePath]:content}
Recommends inspecting files written to disk instead of relying on --dry-run/--print
Explains the Windows backslash imports come from path.relative/toImportStatement and recommends WSL/Linux or normalizing to forward slashes
Says the README is stale/not authoritative for current behavior
